name: Northeast Materials Database (NEMAD) — magnetic materials
description: LLM-extracted magnetic literature records with transition temperatures, magnetization and crystallographic descriptors.
count_scope: Paper release; composition, structural descriptors and magnetic properties define entries
license: Unknown for full website database; processed ML archive declares CC BY 4.0

sources.title: The northeast materials database for magnetic materials
sources.evidence: Publisher/full text reports 67,573 entries and Table 1 units; full database at nemad.org and processed training data on GitHub/Zenodo.

sources.title: NEMAD-MagneticML v1.0 deposit
sources.evidence: Open processed ML release; deposit metadata declares CC BY 4.0. This does not establish the license of the full website corpus.

caveats: Independent extraction release; source literature may overlap CDE Curie–Néel and Starrydata magnetic records, so counts cannot be added as unique materials.

NEMAD is a separate author/provider extraction lineage from Court/Cole ChemDataExtractor/Snowball Curie–Néel releases; literature overlap is plausible and no row-level deduplication or inherited-source equivalence is established.
Crystal structure/lattice/space-group descriptors do not establish complete atomic-coordinate coverage.
Retain experimental-status flag and source DOI; property completeness varies. Website requires JavaScript; full live corpus not exported in this audit.

name: NEMAD / GPTArticleExtractor thermoelectric database
description: Literature-extracted experimental and computational thermoelectric properties with separate measurement temperatures and structural metadata.
count_scope: Published 2025 database cohort; not independently deduplicated compositions

sources.title: Large Language Model-Driven Database for Thermoelectric Materials
sources.evidence: Authors report 7,123 entries from Elsevier literature, approximately 66% from experimental papers. Table 1 provides an experimental/theoretical flag, property-specific temperatures and units; conclusion identifies nemad.org as the open database.

sources.title: Published thermoelectric database paper
sources.evidence: OpenAlex identifies the 2025 Computational Materials Science version of the same named work; not counted separately from preprint.

caveats: Approximately66% of records are experimental; retain the origin flag. Bulk, thin-film and nanostructured material forms are mixed and must remain distinguished.
Same hosting platform as magnetic NEMAD but a separate property corpus; no addition to a global unique-material count.
May overlap Starrydata and ChemDataExtractor thermoelectric source literature.
Experimental-status field must be retained; missing or mixed measurement temperatures cannot be collapsed into one row-level condition.
Descriptive crystal metadata does not guarantee complete atomic coordinates.
Full JavaScript website export and dataset license were not verified.

name: teMatDb272 thermoelectric material database
description: Digitized temperature-dependent transport curves filtered for agreement between reported and recalculated ZT.
count_scope: High-fidelity subset in teMatDb v1.1.6, selected from 355 raw digitized curve sets

sources.title: teMatDb v1.1.6: Thermoelectric Material Database
sources.evidence: Deposit reports 355 raw curve sets and 272 high-fidelity samples; metadata declares CC BY 4.0 and exposes versioned ZIP.

sources.title: A High-Quality Thermoelectric Material Database with Self-Consistent ZT Filtering
sources.evidence: Preprint describes 14,717 temperature-property pairs in 272 sample sets across 262 publications and self-consistent ZT filtering.

caveats: Curve sets and temperature-property pairs are different counting units; neither is a unique-crystal count.
Keep digitized curves, units and individual temperature grids; do not replace them with peak-ZT scalars.
Property units should be read from the released per-property data; the deposit summary does not establish one global stored-unit convention.
Independent digitization may overlap UCSB, ESTM and Starrydata source experiments.

additional_counts.scope: Parent digitized cohort before self-consistent ZT filtering
teMatDb272 as reported by accompanying preprint

name: ESTM experimentally synthesized thermoelectric materials
description: Manually compiled thermoelectric observations released with the SIMD materials representation study.
count_scope: Published ESTM cohort, verified as 5,205 rows × 8 columns in dataset/estm.xlsx
license: Unknown; no dataset-specific or repository license verified

sources.title: A public database of thermoelectric materials and system-identified material representation for data-driven discovery
sources.evidence: Paper reports 5,205 observations for 880 materials, identified by composition and measuring temperature.

sources.title: SIMD primary repository
sources.evidence: README distinguishes full ESTM from a separately distributed Starrydata subset. Downloaded ESTM worksheet has 5,205 rows and explicit units in all property column names.

caveats: ESTM is distinct from the repository's separately included Starrydata slice; do not catalog that slice as another independent source.
880 material count is provider-reported; 5,205 is the observation count.
Power factor and ZT can be derived from measured quantities; preserve this distinction.
No periodic atomic structures are provided in the released worksheet.

additional_counts.scope: Paper-reported compositions represented by the observations

name: WenzhouTE computed thermoelectric database
description: Additional transport and thermomechanical calculations on Materials Project structures using deformation-potential transport and an elastic-model lattice conductivity.
count_scope: Provider homepage cohorts: 1,915 class-1 + 1,692 class-2 calculations
license: Unknown for database; article CC BY 4.0 does not establish data licensing

sources.title: WenzhouTE primary provider homepage
sources.evidence: Homepage states 1,915 calculated materials from class 1 and 1,692 from class 2; the sum is 3,607.

sources.title: Wenzhou TE: A First-Principle-Calculated Thermoelectric Materials Database
sources.evidence: Methods specify PBE/VASP, BoltzTraP2, deformation-potential relaxation times and Slack-formula lattice conductivity; Table 2 labels 300 K transport properties.

caveats: The article reports 1,915 + 1,656 screened materials, while the live homepage reports 1,915 + 1,692. This row uses the homepage snapshot, not the paper total.
Material identities overlap Materials Project; this is a new property calculation release, not 3,607 novel compounds.
Lattice conductivity is a Slack-model estimate from elastic properties, not a full anharmonic BTE calculation.
Carry temperature, carrier concentration, carrier type and approximation with transport values.
Browser search page loads but a full row export was not audited.

count_derivation.method: Sum of disjoint K-means class-1 and class-2 calculated-material cohorts on provider homepage

name: HH130 half-Heusler thermal-transport / MLIP release
description: Compound-specific interatomic potentials and configuration datasets supporting anharmonic thermal transport of half-Heusler crystals.
count_scope: HH130 material-level cohort; thermal-transport study performed on an 80-compound subset
properties: lattice thermal conductivity including four-phonon scattering (W/m/K)
license: Unknown for downloadable data/model archive; article is CC BY-NC 3.0

sources.title: HH130 primary Digital Discovery paper
sources.evidence: Paper describes 130 half-Heuslers, 31,891 configurations and 390 compound-specific models; data-availability statement gives provider ZIP and thermal conductivity analysis for 80 compounds at 300 K.

caveats: Keep material, configuration and model counts separate.
Thermal conductivities include MLIP-based higher-order force constants; they are computed estimates, not measurements.
Only 80 of the 130 compounds enter the reported thermal-transport analysis.
Temperature and phonon-scattering order must accompany conductivity.
Live provider archive accessibility is documented in primary/hh_download_access.json; no archive was downloaded or inspected.
Potential training configurations are a specialized property-supporting release and should not be added to other MLIP datasets as unique structures.
Live provider homepage and archive both returned HTTP 502 during this audit; paper gives a public release route, but current download availability is unresolved.

additional_counts.scope: HH130 training dataset, as reported by paper
Three models for each of 130 compounds

name: DAX-Ti experimental Ti-alloy mechanical-property compilation
description: Composition, phases and processing conditions linked to experimental Ti-alloy stiffness, hardness and strength.

sources.title: A compilation of experimental data on the mechanical properties and microstructural features of Ti-alloys
sources.evidence: Paper reports 282 entries from 105 studies; Table 1 supplies units, reference DOI, phases and treatment conditions; experiments are at room temperature.

sources.title: DAX-Ti static-0.1.0 deposit
sources.evidence: Open CC BY 4.0 deposit exposes static CSV, field definitions and helper script; description identifies 282 distinct alloys.

caveats: Room-temperature alloy properties depend on processing, phases and test method, not composition alone.
Tensile strain is positive and compression strain negative; some nonfracturing specimens have deformation capped at ±50%.
Not every entry contains all properties; oxygen/grain-size coverage is incomplete.
Phase labels are not full periodic atomic structures.

name: Copper-alloy mechanical properties and electrical conductivity (Gorsse 2023)
description: Literature-derived Cu-alloy treatment conditions and mechanical/electrical measurements for precipitation-strengthened alloy design.
count_scope: Published 2023 Cu-alloy CSV release; approximately 150 alloy compositions

sources.title: Dataset of mechanical properties and electrical conductivity of copper-based alloys
sources.evidence: Data Records specify 1,831 records; conditions, target units and source DOI fields are documented. Approximately 150 compositions are represented.

sources.title: Figshare primary dataset metadata
sources.evidence: Public CSV Cu_alloys_database_2023_06_06.csv; metadata declares CC0 and DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.23735373.v1.

caveats: Observation count is not distinct-alloy count.
Microstructure is often insufficiently reported; thermal and thermomechanical processing are retained instead.
Mechanical properties are sparse: paper reports 1,614 hardness, 163 yield-strength, 276 ultimate-strength and 1,826 conductivity records.
May share source experiments with the separate Cu-Cr-X release; no cross-release deduplication performed.
Composition/property tables do not contain full atomic structures.

name: Cu-Cr-X mechanical and electrical property dataset
description: Automated figure extraction linked to manually curated composition, processing and literature metadata for Cu-Cr-X alloys.
count_scope: Paper cohort extracted from 251 figures in 146 papers

sources.title: Mechanical and Electrical Properties dataset of Cu-Cr-X alloys generated with automated figure data extraction
sources.evidence: Paper reports 3,018 records from 251 figures across 146 papers; Figshare JSON/XLSX release and source DOI are documented.

sources.title: Cu-Cr-X Figshare v2 metadata
sources.evidence: Public JSON archive and XLSX available; metadata declares CC BY 4.0 and version DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.29369987.v2.

caveats: A figure-derived record is not an independent composition or unique crystal.
Keep property-unit and treatment metadata per record; extraction and outlier labels remain useful quality evidence.
Shares an application domain and potentially experiments with Gorsse 2023; distinct extraction/release does not imply disjoint data.
Full spreadsheet units and per-property completeness were not independently audited.

name: polyVERSE load-dependent experimental Vickers hardness
description: Experimental indentation hardness with applied load, released separately from DFT-derived hardness proxy rows.
count_scope: Published curated experimental subset; verified as 2,480 data rows in only_exp_data.csv
properties: Vickers hardness (GPa in paper abstract; verify stored-unit convention)
license: Custom Georgia Tech Research Corporation General Public Use License; commercial-gain sale requires separate agreement

sources.title: Load-dependent hardness prediction for materials using machine learning
sources.evidence: Methods report 2,480 unique composition-load records, 69 elements and 514 chemical systems; applied loads span below 2 to above 50 N.

sources.title: polyVERSE primary experimental data CSV
sources.evidence: Downloaded CSV contains 2,480 data rows with composition, load, hardness, category and type fields.

sources.title: polyVERSE GTRC license
sources.evidence: License explicitly includes code, data and documentation; grants redistribution/modification under conditions and requires a separate agreement for commercial-gain sales.

caveats: Repository also provides computed proxy hardness; retain experimental category and do not combine them as measured values.
The article abstract reports GPa but its conclusion reports MPa; CSV column lacks unit metadata. Stored hardness-unit convention needs checking before quantitative harmonization.
Processing/microstructure metadata are largely absent.
Dataset can contain noncrystalline alloy compositions; a crystalline-only subset has not been isolated.
Custom license is not an OSI/Creative-Commons open-data license.

name: LLM-extracted magnetocaloric materials database (Yuan–Yang–Patra–Liao)
description: Magnetocaloric literature records retaining entropy change, magnetic field and transition temperature, with separately curated MP-linked subsets.
count_scope: Current modified6125.csv parsed with Python csv: 6,614 rows excluding header; paper describes 6,615 entries
properties: magnetic entropy change ΔSM (source units; typically J/kg/K)
magnetic field (T or kOe, source field)
source literature metadata for linked subset
license: Unknown; no repository dataset license verified

sources.title: Enhancing Magnetocaloric Material Discovery: A Machine Learning Approach Using an Autogenerated Database by Large Language Models
sources.evidence: Paper reports 6,615 raw entries, 1,426 inorganic-filtered entries and 752 MP matches. ML training normalizes fields to 5 T and uses 229 unique materials.

sources.title: Primary MCE database repository
sources.evidence: README distinguishes raw, inorganic and human-corrected MP-linked releases. Downloaded modified6125.csv parses to 6,614 data rows; updated linked CSV parses to 714 rows.

caveats: Published and current CSV counts disagree (6,615 vs 6,614; 752 MP matches vs 714 rows in current human-corrected linked CSV); filename labels are not trusted counts.
The raw database includes organic and alloyed materials; it is not wholly a periodic inorganic crystal dataset.
Raw field units and string/range values need normalization; field strength strongly affects entropy change.
The paper's linearly scaled 5 T maximum-per-material training values are derived targets, not direct measurements all made at 5 T.
Source abstracts may describe experimental and computed results; retain origin and do not label the entire corpus uniformly experimental.

name: FatigueData-CMA2022 complex metallic-alloy fatigue database
description: Literature-derived stress-life, strain-life and fatigue-crack-growth curves with processing, load and testing conditions.
count_scope: Paper release covering metallic glasses and multi-principal element alloys; not a count of compositions or scalar data points
properties: test temperature, load ratio and environment
license: CC BY 4.0 (Figshare dataset); MIT applies separately to accompanying scripts

sources.title: Fatigue database of complex metallic alloys
sources.evidence: Paper documents 272 test-condition datasets with three fatigue-curve families, material/processing/testing metadata and default MPa stress units.

sources.title: FatigueData-CMA2022 deposit metadata
sources.evidence: Open v2 deposit includes MAT, JSON and XLSX with CC BY 4.0 license.

caveats: Includes amorphous metallic glasses as well as crystalline MPEAs; filter material class for crystal-specific use.
Dataset count differs from number of compositions and curve points; EXCEL curves are sampled to 500 points per dataset while MAT/JSON preserve richer curves.
When unspecified, authors assume uniaxial testing at 25 °C in air and stress concentration Kt=1; these are imputed defaults, not reported measurements.
Use stress ratio, surface/processing state and run-out flags; do not aggregate fatigue values by composition alone.
